Subject: ACME POC: proposed integration plan & success criteria

Hi Samuel —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Per our discussion, attached is a concise POC plan and an initial integration checklist so your engineering and security teams can review. High-level summary below and proposed next steps.

POC objective (2 weeks):
- Validate Redwood inference for in-product suggestions with streaming responses and tool-calling to the search service.
- Demonstrate latency <= 250ms 95th percentile and cost per 1k tokens within target range.

Success criteria (suggested):
1) Functional: 80% of sampled prompts return relevant suggestions compared to current baseline (per your eval set).
2) Performance: p95 latency <= 250ms for single-request streaming in our dedicated dev pool.
3) Reliability: zero data exfiltration, all requests audited in the control plane logs.
4) Integration: SDK-based streaming + tool-calling flow implemented by your engs; end-to-end demo.

Evaluation plan & timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): kickoff & access — exchange API keys, security questionnaire, share onboarding docs.
- Week 1: implement SDK integration, wire streaming endpoints, set up tool-calling to /internal/search.
- Week 2: run evaluation prompts (your set), capture logs/metrics, review results, and adjust.

Ownership (recommended):
- ACME eng lead: Samuel Diaz (implementation)
- Redwood eng SE: Dev Patel (technical onboarding & pairing)
- Customer success: Monica Patel (success criteria & rollout guidance)

Attachments: redwood-poc-plan.pdf, sdk-integration-guide.md
Links: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcDeFGhPocPlan

Next steps:
1) Can we confirm kickoff on Wed 30 Jun at 10:00 PT?
2) Please share the small evaluation prompt set (10-20 examples) and any procurement contact if we'll need an MSA or an SOW.

Happy to adjust criteria based on your priorities — flagged the items that are negotiable.

Best,
Marissa

Hey Sam —

Thanks for the notes — looping in a quick technical sketch of the approaches we discussed. Below are the two recommended patterns: SDK streaming + tool-calling (preferred) and direct REST.

1) SDK streaming (Node example):
- use @redwood/inference SDK, call client.streaming.generate({ model: 'rw-instruct-1', prompt, tools: [{ name: 'acme_search', call: { url: 'https://internal.acme.com/search', auth: 'bearer-short' } }] })
- The SDK opens a websocket for tokens; tool-calls are emitted as structured events with metadata {tool_call: {name, input, id}} which you can subscribe to.
- Auth: server-to-server short-lived JWT; Redwood will accept signed JWTs minted by your auth service or exchange a long-lived key for a short-lived token during kickoff (we can demonstrate).

2) REST streaming (if you can't use SDK):
- POST /v1/streams?model=rw-instruct-1 with Authorization: Bearer <token>
- Server sends events: event: token
- Tool calls: sent as a separate event type: event: tool_call

API routes & telemetry:
- /v1/streams (streaming generation)
- /v1/calls (tool call trigger/ack)
- /v1/metrics (ingestion of evaluation markers)

Attachments: api-endpoints.txt (contains sample cURL and websocket handshake)

If you'd like, I can join the kickoff to walk through a live SDK pairing session.

Cheers,
